text: Professional OverviewGeological engineering focuses on the study of geological bodies such as rocks, soils, and groundwater on the Earth's surface. It primarily explores the structure, properties, and evolution patterns of these geological bodies, as well as how to utilize geological knowledge to avoid risks and optimize designs in engineering projects (such as mineral resource development, water conservancy projects, transportation projects, and geological disaster prevention and control). It is both an extension of geology in the field of engineering and a "geological safety guarantee" discipline for engineering construction.Training ObjectivesThe program aims to cultivate comprehensive engineering professionals with a solid foundation in geology, engineering mechanics, and hydrogeology, who possess professional skills in geological surveying, engineering design, geological hazard assessment and control, and can engage in surveying, design, construction, management, and research in fields such as geological resource development, civil engineering, and environmental engineering. Students are required to have both theoretical analysis skills and field practice abilities, and to focus on solving geological problems in actual engineering projects.Main CoursesBasic Courses: Introduction to Geology, Mineralogy and Petrology, Structural Geology, Geomorphology, Engineering Mechanics, Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, Hydrogeology, etc.Specialized Courses: Geological Surveying Techniques and Methods, Engineering Geology, Geological Hazard Prevention and Control Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering Design, Mineral Resource Development Technology, Geophysical Exploration, Remote Sensing Technology and Application, Geological Engineering Numerical Simulation, etc.Practical Courses: Field Geology Practice (such as regional geological mapping, geological profile measurement), Engineering Survey Practice, Geological Hazard Investigation Practice, etc., emphasizing the combination of theory and field practice.
